name: Solar system rental or lease (residential)
summary: A provider installs and owns a home PV system (often with battery) and the homeowner pays a flat monthly rent over a long term with no upfront cost; installation, maintenance and insurance are included.
how_it_makes_money: Flat monthly lease payments over about 20 years; the provider also can benefit from incentives as owner of the system. Contribution margin was reported positive from the start in the early years.

hardware: Wallbox or heat pump as add-ons
partners: Investors and lenders funding the installed base
regulation: Grid connection with more than 800 grid operators, each with its own process
financing: Provider or investors carry the system cost for years; overleverage is a risk
channel: Aggressive digital performance marketing and in-house sales

stakeholder_value.customer: No upfront cost, flat monthly payment, service included
stakeholder_value.provider: Long-term recurring revenue and a lasting customer relationship

what_must_be_true: Cost of capital is low enough to fund the installed base
Customers accept a very long contract
Installers can be hired or trained fast enough
Rent stays attractive compared with buying as module and storage prices fall

risks_failure_causes.text: Competitors criticised the rental pricing; the provider publicly defended it
Some customers find the 20-year term too long
Falling prices for modules, storage and wallboxes put many providers under pressure and push customers to buy instead
Funding many rented systems up front can leave the provider overleveraged if customers do not use as much energy as projected

cases.note: Offers a 20-year PV rental with no upfront payment. Had about 10,000 lease customers in 2021 and was not yet profitable then. Added an option to buy in 2023.
Cut staff from nearly 400 to just under 50 in six months; the new CEO said the model it had run for nearly a decade would never have become profitable.
